title: swetest: format-sequence output engine (-f)
description:
Port C's `print_line` format-sequence interpreter (swetest.c:2067-2774, ~700 lines). Each character in the `-f` format string produces one output column.

**Format characters** (all 50+):

*Date/time (7)*: `y` year, `Y` year.fraction, `p` planet index, `P` planet name, `J` absolute JD, `T` date `dd.mm.yyyy`, `t` date `yymmdd`

*Ecliptic position (7)*: `L` longitude ddd°mm'ss", `l` longitude decimal, `Z` longitude sign-format (ddsignmm'ss"), `S` speed ddd:mm:ss/day, `s` speed decimal, `B` latitude ddd°mm'ss", `b` latitude decimal

*Distance (5)*: `R` distance AU, `r` distance AU (Moon in parallax seconds), `W` distance light-years, `w` distance km, `q` relative distance (1000=nearest)

*Equatorial (4)*: `A` RA hh:mm:ss, `a` RA decimal, `D` declination ddd°mm'ss", `d` declination decimal

*Horizontal (6)*: `I` azimuth ddd°mm'ss", `i` azimuth decimal, `H` true altitude ddd°mm'ss", `h` true altitude decimal, `K` apparent altitude ddd°mm'ss", `k` apparent altitude decimal

*Cartesian (4)*: `U`/`X` ecliptic x,y,z, `u`/`x` equatorial x,y,z

*Speed modifier (2)*: `SS`/`ss` — print speed for ALL preceding format columns (not just longitude)

*House position (5)*: `Q` house position (Gauquelin), `N`/`n` nodes (asc long/lat), `F`/`f` apsides (peri long/lat)

*Arithmetic (5)*: `+` longitude sum with prior, `-` longitude diff, `*` latitude sum, `/` latitude diff, `=` distance diff

*Special (4)*: `V`/`v` Human Design gates, `m` meridian distance, `z` zenith distance

**Formatting helpers** — reuse existing `swisseph::format` module (`cs2timestr`, `cs2lonlatstr`, `cs2degstr`) plus `swisseph::math::split_deg`. The C `dms()` function is a wrapper around these.

**Output options that modify formatting**:
- `-g` separator (default space, tab if `-g` alone)
- `-dms` use degree-minute-second instead of decimal where applicable
- `-roundsec` / `-roundmin` rounding
- `-ep` extra precision
- `-hor` horizontal listing (all planets on one line, time columns not repeated)

**Key pattern**: The format engine iterates the format string char by char. For each char, it reads from the computed position array (`data[0..6]`) and the supplementary computations (azalt, house position, equatorial coords from `EQUATORIAL` flag or manual conversion). Horizontal/azalt columns require a prior `Ephemeris::azalt()` call. House position requires a prior `Ephemeris::house_pos()` call.

**Output fidelity**: Aim for readable, correct output. Don't spend excessive time matching C's exact field widths and printf padding — that's a polish pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: swetest -b1.1.2000 -p0 -fPLBRS (default) prints planet name, longitude, latitude, distance, speed
All 50+ format characters produce output without panic
-dms flag switches decimal columns to DMS format

execution_record: Implemented in two commits: (1) 2cd06e4 — core format engine with all 50+ format characters, FormatContext/dms()/format_line() architecture, supplementary computation dispatch (equatorial/azalt/cartesian/house_pos/phenomena only when format needs them); (2) b0ccaa5 — N/n/F/f node+apside format chars via nod_aps calls. Output matches C swetest character-for-character on PLBRS, PLBRSAD, PUU, PZ across all default planets. Mean nodes/apsides match bitwise; osculating show the documented fac=z/ż sensitivity (~1e-4°). The -hor horizontal listing mode was deferred to swisseph-rs/149 (it changes the outer loop, not the format engine).
